body.q: A business has revenue of $200 000, cost of sales of $120 000 and expenses of $50 000. What is the gross profit margin?
Using the same figures (revenue $200 000, cost of sales $120 000, expenses $50 000), what is the profit margin (profit for the year as a percentage of revenue)?
A business has current assets of $45 000 (including inventory of $15 000) and current liabilities of $30 000. What is the current ratio?
body.why: Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities = $45 000 / $30 000 = 1.5 : 1.

body.q: Using the same figures (current assets $45 000 including inventory $15 000, current liabilities $30 000), what is the liquid (acid test) ratio?
body.why: Liquid ratio = (current assets - inventory) / current liabilities = $30 000 / $30 000 = 1 : 1.

body.q: A business has capital employed of $250 000 and profit from operations of $40 000. What is the return on capital employed (ROCE)?
body.why: ROCE = profit from operations / capital employed x 100 = $40 000 / $250 000 x 100 = 16%.

body.q: A business has an opening inventory of $18 000, a closing inventory of $22 000 and a cost of sales of $160 000. What is the rate of inventory turnover?
A business has trade receivables of $30 000 and credit sales of $240 000 for the year. How many days on average do customers take to pay?
body.why: Trade receivable days = $30 000 / $240 000 x 365 = 45.6, which rounds to 46 days.

body.q: Which of the following actions would most likely improve a business's current ratio?
body.why: Where the ratio is above 1, repaying a current liability with a current asset reduces both by the same amount and increases the ratio.

body.q: A business's profit margin has fallen from 18% to 12% while its gross profit margin has stayed the same. What is the most likely reason?
body.why: If gross profit margin is unchanged, the fall in profit margin must be caused by higher expenses relative to revenue.

body.q: Which ratio would a bank manager mainly use to assess whether a business can pay its short-term debts as they fall due?
body.why: The liquid ratio measures the ability to meet short-term liabilities from the most easily converted current assets.
